title: Retail loan book: early arrears trend

findings.headline: Early arrears have nearly doubled since Q2 2025
findings.detail: The share of loans 30+ days past due at 6 months was 6.6% for Q2 25 loans and 12.8% for Q1 26 loans (12.8 ÷ 6.6 ≈ 1.9 times). It has risen in each of the last three quarters, from 7.8% to 9.7% to 12.8%.

findings.headline: Deterioration is concentrated in Personal and Card loans
findings.detail: Personal loans went from 8.7% in Q2 25 to 21.0% in Q1 26, and Card from 12.2% to 20.2%. Car stayed near 6% and Home near 0.5%.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high missed payments
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 rows. 83.3% of those rows were 30+ days past due at 6 months, against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment, against 2.3% overall. This looks like a possible fraud or application-duplication signal.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed borrowers show higher arrears
findings.detail: Digital loans run at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch. Self-employed borrowers run at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried. These are patterns, not proven causes, and may overlap with the Personal and Card mix.

findings.headline: Income is missing for 39.7% of Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is 6.9% missing overall, and 90.8% of the gaps are in the Partner channel. Any income-based analysis or rule will be weaker for that channel.

next_steps: Split Q1 26 Personal and Card arrears by channel, employment and loan size to find which part of the new lending is driving the rise.
Refer the 42 loans sharing phone values to fraud review, and check whether the same applicants or partners appear in them.
Confirm every Q4 25 and Q1 26 loan has a full 6 months of history, and ask Partner sourcing why income is missing.

conclusion: Early arrears are clearly worsening, from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, and the rise sits mainly in Personal and Card lending. Do first: break down recent Personal and Card loans by channel, employment and loan size to find where the weakness is. Then review the 42 loans sharing phone numbers and fix the missing Partner income.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show why arrears are rising, whether the recent quarters have a full 6 months of history, or whether the channel, employment and product patterns overlap.
